Roofing QA — inspection read-out
Actual project state
Project: New project, revision 1, design revision 1, pane sheets.
Active document: doc-sample — No source plan (bundled sample), sha256: null, page count 1.
Source candidates: 1 sample entry, no governing sources, informationStatus: unknown.
Evidence on sheet 1: calibration unlocked, source unverified, confidence 0, no known distance, no traces, no located items, no annotations.
Attachments: none stored. Price books: none imported.
Save state: savedProjectRevision = 1, recovery not blocked, no save error.
Architectural controller: not mounted (Sketch/Architectural workspace would need navigate_workspace pane: sketch first, but no edits were requested).
Can a source-backed pitched-roof takeoff run right now?

No. A source-backed takeoff requires all of the following, none of which are satisfied:

A governing source — the only document is a sample placeholder with no SHA-256, so source identity cannot match.
A locked two-point calibration on the target sheet — sheet 1 reports locked: false, knownDistanceM: null, candidates: 0.
Actual roof geometry to trace — the read returned no traces, and the sample has no identified walls, ridges, eaves, hips or valleys to follow.
Stated dimensions from the user — no user-supplied known distance or roof specification exists in this session.
Decision owner / professional authority — unverified, so even if lengths were traced they could not be approved or issued here.

The blockers the evidence itself reports match exactly: “Import or select a source document,” “Confirm and lock the drawing scale for sheet 1,” and “Trace at least one takeoff run.”

What the available tools can do (read-only here)
read_project_context ✔ used — confirms identity and source list.
read_source_sheets ✔ used — sample sheets refused to organise, which is the expected firewall.
read_takeoff_evidence ✔ used — surfaces calibration, traces, items and blockers per sheet.
read_assistant_file ✔ used (listing) — no project files present.
read_price_books ✔ used — no rate books imported.
read_workflow_route ✔ used — inspect route selected, no permissions granted.
What is not available through tools
Importing a plan is UI-only; I cannot attach a real roof plan in this session.
No quote, bill-of-materials, areas or volumes are produced from a sample.
No editing, drawing, calibration, trace, approval or export was performed — by request, and because the prerequisites are absent.
prepare_source_room / read_source_geometry need a real attached source page; the active one is a sample placeholder.
Tools / actions actually executed
read_workflow_route (inspect).
read_project_context.
read_source_sheets.
read_takeoff_evidence.
read_assistant_file (listing).
read_price_books.
Conclusion

This session can deliver a roofing-QA inspection report (the read-out above), but it cannot deliver a source-backed pitched-roof takeoff. The first roof run would require, in order: attach a real PDF/DXF source with a known SHA-256, lock a two-point scale calibration on the target sheet with the user’s known distance, then trace each ridge/eave/hip/valley and rafter run before any length, area or count is quoted.

Developer review
Outcome: Honest inspection — stated that the sample source and unlocked calibration block any source-backed takeoff, without fabricating measurements.
Friction: None in execution; the user’s prerequisites (real source, user-stated scale, roof dimensions) genuinely cannot be supplied through tools, so further calls would only repeat evidence.
Improvement: Could open with a one-line yes/no before the detail block to let a busy reviewer decide at a glance; the rest was clear and correctly separated from the developer section.
